scope: Empirical language usability; no language implementation or acceptance

claims.statement: U01 Study 4 analyzes 72 novice participants across six language conditions; Ruby, Python and Quorum outperform Randomo on token accuracy, while Java and Perl do not show a significant advantage over Randomo. Most real-language pairwise differences are not significant.
limitations: Novice short tasks; token accuracy; language-feature bundles; a non-significant contrast is not equivalence.

claims.statement: Adapt familiar declaration forms for a defined audience, while testing semantic interpretation independently of punctuation.
limitations: Neither paper evaluates TypeScript or finance developers.
claims.proposed_test: Compare semantically equivalent financial clauses, stratifying by prior TypeScript and functional-language experience.

claims.statement: U01 intuition surveys had 166 respondents each with some overlap; generic-syntax ratings were inconclusive.
limitations: Ratings are not task performance; self-reported experience.

claims.statement: U02 Auction correct completion was 7/10 Obsidian versus 2/10 Solidity. The p≈0.015 comparison conditions on claimed completion; the all-participant comparison was p≈0.070.
limitations: 20 analyzed Java programmers; one long-tutorial participant excluded; short training and task.

claims.statement: In U02 Casino, all four Obsidian participants with compiling completed programs misused disown; none had a fully correct solution. One Solidity participant had a fully correct solution.
limitations: Variable remaining task time; difficult task; one compiler-bug case discarded; not a population effect estimate.

claims.statement: Defer general unchecked escape hatches; evaluate whether repair attempts discard obligations or assets to silence diagnostics.
limitations: Moriarty is not Obsidian; scoped language semantics require separate design justification.
claims.proposed_test: Observe seeded residual-duty and asset-loss repairs, including requests for unchecked casts or suppressed checks.

claims.statement: U04 retained 27 of 33 recruited students. Static typing favored three API tasks and dynamic typing two; the task-specific analysis does not establish a universal type-system winner.
limitations: Java-familiar students; carryover; exclusions; stripped-static Groovy API; no mainstream IDE feature comparison.

claims.statement: Adapt explicit type information at public financial boundaries and study inferred locals separately from erasing types.
limitations: Annotations and checking are confounded in this study; inference was future work.
claims.proposed_test: Equal-signature explicit-local versus inferred-local condition with type display; measure navigation, mistakes and repair time.

claims.statement: U05 message quizzes had 27 complete cases: incorrect interpretation was 17.28% for standard messages and 6.17% for enhanced messages, with reported paired-test p<0.035.
limitations: Message comprehension outside programming context; does not estimate secure repair.

claims.statement: U05 think-aloud programming study did not show a substantial overall learning-outcome improvement, despite observations of useful reading and edits in response to enhanced messages.
limitations: 31 sessions; historical semester comparison; compiler access, prior-code access and teacher differences.

claims.statement: Adopt separate measures of diagnostic comprehension, correct repair, recurrence and suppression attempts.
limitations: Friendly wording alone is not a demonstrated productivity intervention.
claims.proposed_test: Seed wrong-asset, recipient, fee and rounding errors; measure first edit and eventual correct obligation-preserving repair.

claims.statement: U06 Table 4 reports DSL/GPL success means of 57.62/40.95 learning, 64.57/50.86 perceiving, 70.95/33.33 evolving, and 64.34/43.37 overall, in percent.
limitations: 35 retained students; GUI questionnaire comparison, not production coding.

claims.statement: U06 conclusion summarizes roughly 15% improvement across categories; Table 4 instead gives 16.67, 13.71 and 37.62 percentage-point differences, and 20.97 overall. Use explicit table numbers.
limitations: No raw-data reanalysis; publisher discrepancy preserved.

claims.statement: U06 inferential statistics require caution: its prose calls the test independent although participants answered both questionnaires; cognitive-dimension attribution assumes equal contribution among selected dimensions.
limitations: This is a methodological limitation identified from the paper, not a reanalysis or disproof of its directional observation.

claims.statement: Adapt domain-specific financial vocabulary, but defer importing the GUI study effect size into finance.
limitations: One domain and two specific notations; prior familiarity uneven.
claims.proposed_test: Compare equivalent partial-payment and rounding-policy edits; include duty survival and wrong-recipient detection.

claims.statement: U09 pilot uses 18 respondents: ten unsupervised and eight interviewed. Respondents identify concrete usability issues, but group, questionnaire and interview differences prevent a clean causal comparison.
limitations: Small convenience pilot, no validated scalar language ranking.

claims.statement: Adopt cognitive-dimension prompts for visibility, dependencies, change effort and role clarity; defer a summed score ranking entire languages.
limitations: Usability concerns notation plus environment.
claims.proposed_test: Ask reviewers to locate all clauses affected by an asset-unit, rounding-policy or residual-duty change.

claims.statement: U10 reports eight student designers and six completed projects; spontaneous syntax choices and actual task failures reveal prior-experience effects and mistaken designer assumptions.
limitations: Qualitative convenience studies; end-user counts not consistently specified; no final-language performance trial.

claims.statement: Adapt natural-programming tasks as formative evidence, followed by trained tasks on the actual constrained semantics.
limitations: Spontaneously invented syntax is not proof of learnability or safety.
claims.proposed_test: Elicit an asset-bound limit, partial repayment and delayed claim before teaching spelling; then test interpretation and repair.

claims.statement: Do content-addressed definitions and explicit dependency identity improve financial-language maintenance compared with name/version-oriented modules?
limitations: None of these seven works directly evaluates Unison or content addressing.
claims.proposed_test: Compare rename and dependency-update tasks with equivalent semantic checks; track mistaken assumptions about what changed.

claims.statement: U02 describes both Glacier programming-task contrasts as significant, but one reported p≈0.077 exceeds the conventional 0.05 threshold; retain counts and precise p-values.
limitations: No reanalysis; do not call this contrast significant at 0.05.

claims.statement: Positive bounded-task results and negative open-ended outcomes can coexist; language evaluations should preserve correctness, completion and time as distinct outcomes.
limitations: Heterogeneous tasks and populations; no pooled effect estimate warranted.
